author: WP10
summary: In the working tree this unit is a short overview of the three Emscripten-only 2D browser families (CANVAS, HTML_DOM, SVG_DOM) and of what browser evidence can and cannot show; the retired-family material it once held was removed before the synchronisation. Every claim is current at 009d40f5, and Tutorial 105 already covers each one in more depth (what each renderer emits, readback, testing tiers, choosing), so the unit is absorbed as preserved knowledge.

concepts.text: CANVAS, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM are three Emscripten-only 2D families that do not use WebGL: Canvas replays sprites into a Canvas 2D context, HTML_DOM uses pooled CSS-transformed elements and SVG_DOM maintains SVG nodes; they share the SpriteBatch vocabulary but differ in objects, clipping, blending and readback.

concepts.text: CANVAS batches already-ordered sprite commands across the WebAssembly-to-JavaScript boundary and replays them as drawImage, putImageData and fill operations; it is the one DOM-free browser 2D renderer with a synchronous backbuffer readback.
concepts.note: Phase 5 (c1c316b9): RRC-018 (1cac65958) retired the renderer identities it describes; was PRESERVED. The site keeps no public trace (audit/c1c316b9-phase5-delta.md §3).

concepts.text: CANVAS evidence is source and structural C++ tests only: CNA's Node-based test runner provides no CanvasRenderingContext2D, so no browser pixel run exists and claims stop short of pixel-verified.

concepts.text: HTML_DOM draws sprites as pooled elements with CSS transforms and background images, and is the browser renderer with real automatic headless-Chromium checks of DOM structure, screenshots, timing and memory (htmldom-ci.yml).

concepts.text: On HTML_DOM (and SVG_DOM) RenderTarget2D is backed by a real off-screen canvas so its readback works, the backbuffer readback throws, and unsupported 3D, depth/stencil and MSAA construction throws deterministically.

concepts.text: SVG_DOM keeps one SVG surface with ordered groups and pooled image or pattern nodes per visible sprite; tint is an SVG feColorMatrix filter while opacity stays a separate property.

concepts.text: A successful Emscripten link proves neither DOM availability nor browser lifecycle, layout, paint, compositing or pixels: the multi-renderer web workflow links and inspects WEBGL2, CANVAS, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM together but runs none of them, so a browser claim needs a harness that names the real browser, asserts the selected family, separates DOM inspection from screenshots and records skips.
concepts.note: Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: the destination now says the multi-renderer web workflow pins an sharp-runtime revision that cannot configure at this snapshot (CNA-BUG-199), so it is configured evidence, not a passing run (audit finding C11 ch66-F1 / C06 ch27-F4).

concepts.text: WEBGL1, WEBGL2 and the browser route of WEBGPU are programmable-GPU families; CANVAS, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM are intentionally 2D browser models, so anything past the 2D boundary belongs on WEBGL2.
